summary: Intermittent upstream runtime handshake failures during tenant burst causing elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using BrightWrite Labs (dedicated tenant) reported a sudden increase in 5xx errors during a high-concurrency burst from their mobile clients. Errors started ~2026-03-12 11:18 UTC and persisted intermittently for ~90 minutes.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx rate (~18% of requests for tenant) across short-streaming and small-chat routes.
- Customer reported degraded user experience for ~2k active users during the window.

Environment:
- Production (dedicated pool) in us-east
- Tenant pinned to redwood-open-7b-v1

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Rapidly open 500 short streaming sessions (50 concurrent bursts) from mobile SDK with keepalive disabled in some versions.
2. Send short prompts (~20-40 tokens).
3. Observe ~10-20% of sessions receiving server 502/503.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returning 502/503 with upstream error message: "upstream handshake timeout" or "upstream reset during handshake".
- Some runtime instances (ephemeral pool) restarted with SIGABRT and TLS handshake logs showing timeouts.

Initial logs (excerpt):
- apigw: "ERROR upstream handshake timeout tenant=brightwrite session_id=..."
- proxy: "tls: accept failed: EOF while waiting for client hello"
- runtime: "panic: unexpected EOF during accept (tls handshake)"

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Customer throttled client-side connection ramp (reduced concurrency by 80%) which reduced observed 5xx rate.

Attachments:
- link to Grafana tenant error-rate panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant/brightwrite/error-rate
- support logs bundle: s3://support-logs/sup-365999/2026-03-12.zip
comments: 2026-03-12 11:25 - Aisha Patel: Customer reported sudden 5xx spike. Reproduced with small local load generator. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-12 11:42 - SRE (Marcus Nguyen): Observed handshake timeouts on ephemeral proxy and TLS accept failures on several runtime shards. Opening investigation in #support and #infra-ephemeral.
2026-03-12 12:10 - Ops (Leah Kim): Looked at accept-queue metrics; accept backlog spiked just before handshake timeouts. Possible half-open connection stampede from mobile SDK variant.

2026-03-12 12:45 - Eng (Ravi Desai): Identified runtime goroutine watchdog logs correlating with "tls: handshake timeout" followed by forced restarts from the health manager. Suspect connection handling regression in new accept loop optimization.
2026-03-12 13:20 - Aisha Patel: Customer applied client-side throttle (80% reduction) and error rate dropped to ~2%. Asked for recommended fixes and ETA.
2026-03-13 09:05 - Marcus Nguyen: Deployed temporary config change raising accept_queue_size and re-enabling exponential-backoff on proxy handshake retries for rented ephemeral pool. Monitoring.

2026-03-14 10:12 - Marcus Nguyen: Patch landed in runtime (PR-9982) to harden handshake path and avoid panic on mid-accept EOF. Backported to dedicated release branch and applied during low-traffic window. Marking resolved pending customer confirmation.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 11:15 UTC: observed tenant throughput ramp from client-side telemetry
- 11:18 UTC: API gateway error-rate climbs from baseline 0.5% to 18%
- 11:20-11:35 UTC: accept queue depth grows; apigw logs report 'upstream handshake timeout'
- 11:30 UTC: several runtime shards restarted by health manager (SIGABRT)

Findings:
- Root correlation appears to be a mobile SDK bug that disables keepalive for a subset of clients, causing many short-lived TCP connections with incomplete TLS handshakes under high concurrency.
- The runtime accept path had an optimization that assumed short handshake latencies; under half-open client behavior it hit an unexpected EOF path and triggered a panic in the TLS accept handler. That panic surfaced to process exits on some runtime replicas.
- Ephemeral proxy was not applying backpressure early enough; the accept queue filled and API gateway observed upstream timeouts, returning 502/503 to callers.
- No evidence of GPU OOM or model kernel faults; serving runtime CPU usage increased modestly due to TLS work and goroutine churn.

Diagnostics collected:
- tcpdump traces from proxy replicas showing many SYN packets with no full TLS ClientHello follow-up
- runtime core dumps indicating panic in tls_accept.go: line ~142 (EOF during read)
- Grafana dashboards: accept_queue_size, apigw.upstream_handshake_timeouts, runtime.uptime_restarts

Hypothesis validated:
- Reproduced locally by disabling keepalive and ramping connection open/close at scale — caused identical handshake-timeout patterns and runtime panics.
resolution:
Short-term mitigations applied:
1) Raised ephemeral proxy accept_queue_size and tuned handshake retry/backoff to shed connections earlier. Deployed the change 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC.
2) Customer applied client-side throttling as a stop-gap and confirmed reduced errors.
3) Rolled out runtime patch (PR-9982) that guards against EOF during accept and converts the path to graceful handshake failure instead of panic. Backported to dedicated branch and deployed 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC to low-traffic nodes.

Long-term follow-ups (tracked as action items):
- TASK-1204: Improve accept-queue autoscale policy to proactively rate-limit handshakes on sudden connection ramps.
- TASK-1205: Add an SLI for 'handshake failure rate' and alert at 1% per-tenant sustained for 5m.
- DOCS-88: Publish recommended mobile SDK connection guidance (keepalive enabled, exponential backoff).

Customer outcome:
- BrightWrite Labs confirmed normal traffic patterns on 2026-03-14 and observed error rate returned to baseline (~0.4%). Customer thanked support for patch and advised to wait 48h of stability before closing.
follow_up_items: TASK-1204 - autoscale and rate-limit tuning for accept queues
TASK-1205 - handshake SLI and alert rule
public_status_message: We identified and fixed a runtime handshake edge-case that, combined with a client-side connection ramp, caused elevated 5xx rates for one tenant. We deployed mitigations and a runtime patch; customer error rates returned to baseline. We are adding monitoring and documentation to prevent recurrence.
